points.text: Methods described in Section 3 are hard to map to methods evaluated in Section 4
Unclear which techniques are novel versus existing (max-activation descriptions, logit lens)
Needs qualitative examples of annotator inputs and resulting labels per method
Sentences are long and hard to read
Paper lacks clear narrative and stated claims; bolded takeaway format ineffective
Puri et al. evaluation metrics described too briefly
LLM-as-judge metrics not validated against human annotations
Baselines Neuronpedia and MaxAct* insufficiently described
Unclear whether method works on other sparse dictionaries such as SAEs
Computational cost of techniques, especially circuit analyses, not reported
No implementation available for nontrivial methods
Techniques may be too niche and expensive for practical use
Motivation and explanation of Assumption 2 unclear
Motivation and explanation of circuit-based clustering unclear
Faithfulness scores very low, questioning whether interpretations reflect feature behavior
CircuitLens still requires secondary LLM and large dataset, contradicting core motivation
Figure 1 uninformative; should be expanded with subfigures for each step
Section 3.2 circuit analysis poorly contextualized relative to overall goal
Section 3.2 workflow hard to follow; should be reorganized in logical order
Evaluation reported for only four layers; need all layers
Evaluation criteria not aggregated into single score for comparing configurations
Headline 'matches or exceeds' claims overstated; purity worse for WeightLens in Table 1
CircuitLens with full-distribution sampling below baselines in parts of Table 2
Best CircuitLens results use top-activation sampling, undercutting full-distribution argument
Claim that circuits uncover patterns invisible to activation methods weakly supported
Evaluation scale small: ~250 features per layer, four layers, one model
No confidence intervals, seeds or significance tests; small differences treated as meaningful
Feature selection procedure unclear, possibly including dead features
FADE metrics are LLM-in-the-loop with possible format bias; no human evaluation
WeightLens comparison subset unclear, risking circularity or unfair comparison; report covered/uncovered separately
Assumptions 1 and 2 asserted but not tested
Z-score outlier threshold value and sensitivity unjustified for non-Gaussian projections
Validation step reintroduces dataset dependence, weakening data-free claim
'Semantically aligned' part of Assumption 2 not operationalised
RoPE explanation for mid-layer drop speculative and untested
Attention attributions not causally validated by ablation or patching
No evaluation of cluster quality or comparison with embedding-based clustering
No ablation of rho, DBSCAN parameters or sample count
Cluster counts not shown to reflect real polysemanticity
Gains from combining WeightLens and CircuitLens small
Method improvement confounded with prompt change; no prompt-matched baseline
Faithfulness near zero everywhere, non-discriminative; explanation untested
Output-centric component costly and its benefit shown only anecdotally
Proposed metric modification for circuits not carried out
Missing baselines: other weight-based or logit-lens methods
Scalability and efficiency claims not quantified
24M-token versus large-corpus comparison confounds method with dataset
Typos such as 'WeigthLens' and table value errors
Much key evidence relegated to appendix
